html:
SMTO-ART-0020 — These files are still used by another conversation

GUID: b128263e-79f3-4fba-bb03-53ce0c42b11f
Slug: artifact-retained-references
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO didn't delete these Task files because another conversation still uses them, for example one started with Continue in new conversation. The files are still there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find conversations that begin with a 'Continued from previous conversation' or 'Context from previous task' card whose View source link opens this conversation. Conversations continued from this one can still open its Task files, so SMTO keeps them.
  2. If you no longer need that other conversation's files, open it and choose Delete artifacts or Delete everything from its Retention menu. This removes that conversation's use of the shared files.
  3. Come back to this conversation and choose the same delete option from its Retention menu again. Once no other conversation uses the files, SMTO can delete them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows 'Retention action completed.' and the Task's file list says the files from this run have been deleted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, naming both conversations. Don't delete the files from the server's disk by hand; the other conversation would lose files it still uses.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact retirement or purge was refused because another conversation holds an artifact grant on the run (for example a task fork) or native_artifact_links from runs outside the deletion set still reference its artifacts.

What this means

  • Retirement/purge finds grants from another conversation or retained artifact links from runs outside the selected deletion set. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Retirement/purge finds grants from another conversation or retained artifact links from runs outside the selected deletion set.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact foreign grants and continuation/source links before selecting cleanup scope.

How to fix it

  • List artifact_grants for the run whose conversation_id differs from the purging conversation, and native_artifact_links whose source_run_id is this run but whose run_id is outside the selected conversation. Purge artifacts or everything in those referencing conversations first (which removes their grants and links), then repeat the purge; do not delete grant or link rows directly.
  • Inspect and deliberately remove the retained references through supported conversation controls before deleting shared files.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported deliberate reference removal and settlement make the intended files eligible for deletion.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
